evals.name: cross-document-contradiction
evals.setup: `docs/manual.md` calls Acme "a hosted web platform" in the intro and says "Acme runs entirely in your web browser" three sections later, repeating the browser claim twice more after that. No mode word is given.
expected_behavior: Defaults to audit: models the whole document before judging and edits nothing before approval
Reports the contradiction as a Blocker citing both locations, not just the later one
Flags the twice-repeated browser claim as redundancy
Numbers the findings and groups them Blocker / Should-fix / Nit

evals.name: flag-dubious-claim
evals.setup: `docs/api-guide.md` is clean prose apart from one line asserting "REST APIs are stateful by design."
expected_behavior: Fixes grammar, terminology, and clarity directly in the file
Does not silently rewrite the dubious claim — raises it as a question stating what it would expect instead and why
Lists the flagged claim among the items awaiting the user's decision
Invents no replacement fact it cannot ground

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: An audit of `docs/manual.md` whose findings the user then approves.
expected_behavior: The report opens with the findings — no "I'll now review…" preamble and no step narration
Each finding is stated once; no closing summary re-lists findings already shown
After applying the fixes, states the edit classes and the file path
Does not paste the document back into chat

evals.name: create-grounded-manual
evals.setup: A billing dashboard with no user documentation. The repo shows the screens and the API but says nothing about who uses it or which tasks matter.
evals.query: /doc-smith create a user manual for the billing dashboard
expected_behavior: Fixes audience, product, and purpose, asking only the gaps it cannot infer — audience, key tasks, terminology — in one batched round
Uses one term per concept from the first line and a task-oriented structure (overview → prerequisites → tasks → reference → troubleshooting), omitting empty sections
Runs the whole-document self-review before writing
Writes the file, states the path, and does not paste the manual back

evals.name: drift-across-a-set
evals.setup: Three files meant as one manual. `docs/install.md` calls the unit a "workspace"; `docs/config.md` calls the same thing a "project". `docs/usage.md` points the reader at a "Backup" section that none of the three contains.
evals.query: /doc-smith audit docs/install.md docs/config.md docs/usage.md as one manual
expected_behavior: Treats the three files as one document and checks consistency across all of them, not file by file
Flags workspace/project as terminology drift, naming both files
Flags the missing Backup section as a completeness gap — a dangling reference, not a wording nit

evals.name: revise-keeps-the-whole-coherent
evals.setup: `docs/guide.md` uses "workspace" throughout. While revising an early paragraph the user renames it to "project". Later paragraphs still say "workspace".
expected_behavior: Infers revise mode; moves in document order one paragraph at a time, applying only what the user agrees to and never batch-editing the file
After the rename lands, runs the coherence check and flags the later "workspace" paragraphs as now-inconsistent before moving on
Reports each turn as the proposed change plus the coherence-check result — not a reprint of the document

evals.name: normalize-to-the-doc-s-own-convention
evals.setup: `docs/guide.md` mixes "colour" and "color" and carries a Markdown table whose columns no longer line up. The file's own prose wraps at 100 columns.
expected_behavior: Normalizes to one spelling variety — US by default, but keeps British and flags the mix if the doc is consistently British
Re-aligns the table columns and reflows to the doc's own 100-column wrap, not an imposed house default
Reports the variety mix as a spelling-variety defect
States edit classes and counts without pasting the document back
